title: The Valeoran Ruins
subtitle: The impossible structures above the still ocean, where the Gates form
summary: Enormous ancient structures suspended between Sea and Sky far from any shore, held up by nothing anyone can explain. The Gates form among them.
content:
> *"Valeoran is a designation, not an identification."*
> — a Vernan archaeologist's habitual correction

The **Valeoran Ruins** are enormous ancient structures suspended above a still ocean, far from any trade route, shore or explored land, and held in place by nothing anyone can explain. They're the reason [[endros|Endros]] exists, and the place where the [[gates|Gates]] form.

They were found eleven years ago by a University of Verna vessel taking oceanographic measurements, far beyond any charted horizon, which is why nobody had seen them before. Its scholars thought of an old myth at once, of [[valeor|Valeor]] lifting the Sky away from the Sea, and called them Valeoran. The name means *reminiscent of Valeor*. It doesn't mean Valeor built them, and nothing suggests the builders had anything to do with the myth. Vernan archaeologists have spent years explaining this. (*"There was a poet on the survey team."*)

Who built them, what they are and how they stay up is unknown. A few Vardic enthusiasts tie them to the Nameless King of their folklore, Tianzhao scholars read them through the Spirit Realm, and taverns in Endros have plenty of other theories. None of it is established.

The Ruins themselves are the business of the University of Verna's **Department of Archaeology**. Any work on, under or against a Valeoran structure needs its written approval, and its notices end:

> *If you are unsure whether something is part of the Ruins, it is.*
